title: Triangle & angle theorems
blurb: Each theorem is one move. Spot the shape, then make the move.

anglesum.name: Angle sum of a triangle
anglesum.phrase: Three corners make a straight line: 180°.
steps: Add the angles you know.
Take that from 180°.
What is left is the missing angle.
anglesum.exception: This is for flat paper. A triangle drawn on a ball can add to more than 180°. The outside angles, one at each corner, add to 360°.

exterior.name: Exterior angle
exterior.phrase: The outside angle equals the two far insides.
steps: Find the outside angle at one corner.
Add the two inside angles that do not touch it.
They match.
exterior.exception: Do not use the inside angle next to it. That pair sits on a straight line and makes 180°.

iso.name: Isosceles triangle
steps: Find the two equal sides (the tick marks).
The angles at the bottom of those sides are equal.
Use 180° for the rest.
iso.exception: The twin angles sit across from the twin sides, at the base. The angle between the twin sides is usually different, unless all three sides match.

pythag.name: Pythagoras
pythag.phrase: Square the legs, add them, and that is the long side squared.
pythag.also: a² + b² = c², and c is across from the square corner.
steps: Find the right angle. The side across from it is c.
Square the two legs and add them.
Take the square root. To find a leg, subtract instead: c² − a².
pythag.exception: Only for right triangles. And c is across from the right angle, not just the side that looks longest.

parallel.name: Parallel lines
parallel.phrase: F angles copy, Z angles copy, C angles make 180°.
steps: Trace the letter the two angles make with the lines.
F (corresponding) or Z (alternate): the angles are equal.
C (co-interior): the angles add to 180°.
parallel.exception: Only when the lines are parallel (the arrow marks). Without parallel lines, the angles are not forced to match.

congruent.name: Congruent triangles
congruent.phrase: Same size and shape: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS.
steps: SSS: three sides match.
SAS: two sides and the angle between them.
ASA: two angles and the side between them.
RHS: right angle, hypotenuse, and one more side.
congruent.exception: SSA is not a test: two sides and an angle that is not between them can make two different triangles. AAA shows the same shape but not the same size.

quad.name: Quadrilateral angles
quad.phrase: Four corners make a full turn: 360°.
steps: Add the three angles you know.
Take that from 360°.
quad.exception: Opposite angles are only equal in a parallelogram. Do not assume a shape is a square because it has four sides.

polyint.name: Polygon interior angles
steps: Count the sides n.
A polygon splits into n − 2 triangles from one corner.
Each triangle is 180°, so the interior sum is (n − 2) × 180°.
For a regular polygon, each interior angle is that sum ÷ n.
polyint.exception: n must be at least 3. Exterior angles are a different story: they always sum to 360°, not (n − 2) × 180°.

polyext.name: Exterior angles of a polygon
polyext.phrase: Walk around the shape: exterior angles always add to 360°.
steps: At each corner, the exterior is the turn you make.
All the turns make one full spin: 360°.
For a regular n-gon, each exterior angle is 360° ÷ n.
Interior and exterior at a corner sit on a straight line: they add to 180°.
polyext.exception: This is one exterior at each vertex, all the same way around. Do not mix interior sums with exterior sums.

straight.name: Angles on a line and around a point
straight.phrase: On a line: 180°. Around a point: 360°. Vertically opposite: equal.
steps: Angles on a straight line add to 180°.
Angles around a point add to 360°.
When two lines cross, vertically opposite angles are equal.
straight.exception: Adjacent angles on a cross are not equal — they make 180°. Only the ones across from each other match.

slope.name: Slope
steps: Pick two points on the line.
Rise = change in y (up is positive).
Run = change in x (right is positive).
Slope m = rise ÷ run.
slope.exception: A horizontal line has slope 0 (rise 0). A vertical line has no slope (run 0 — you cannot divide by 0). Count the direction: down means negative rise.

ymxb.name: Slope-intercept form
ymxb.phrase: y = mx + b: m is the slope, b is where it hits the y-axis.
steps: Read m: the number in front of x (slope).
Read b: the constant term (y-intercept).
To find y, plug in x. To find x, plug in y and solve.
ymxb.exception: If the equation is not solved for y, rearrange first. The intercept is on the y-axis (x = 0), not the x-axis.

expLaws.name: Laws of exponents
expLaws.phrase: Multiply → add powers. Divide → subtract. Power of a power → multiply.
steps: xᵃ × xᵇ = xᵃ⁺ᵇ.
xᵃ ÷ xᵇ = xᵃ⁻ᵇ.
(xᵃ)ᵇ = xᵃᵇ.
x⁰ = 1 (for x ≠ 0).
expLaws.exception: The bases must match before you add or subtract powers. (x²)³ is x⁶, not x⁵. And 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷, not 4⁷.

sci.name: Scientific notation
sci.phrase: One digit, then a dot, times a power of ten.
steps: Move the dot until one non-zero digit sits in front.
Count how many places you moved: that is the power of 10.
Left moves give a positive power; right moves give a negative power.
sci.exception: The front number must be at least 1 and less than 10. 34 × 10³ is not scientific notation — write 3.4 × 10⁴.

cylvol.name: Cylinder volume
cylvol.phrase: Cylinder volume is the circle floor times the height: πr²h.
steps: Find the radius r of the circular base.
Area of the base: πr².
Multiply by the height h.
Use π ≈ 3.14.
cylvol.exception: Use radius, not diameter. If you are given the diameter, halve it first. Volume is not surface area.

conevol.name: Cone volume
conevol.phrase: A cone is one-third of the cylinder with the same base and height.
steps: Same base and height as a cylinder would give πr²h.
A cone fills only one-third of that: V = (1/3)πr²h.
Use π ≈ 3.14.
conevol.exception: Do not forget the 1/3. Comparing a cone to a cylinder only works when r and h match.

spherevol.name: Sphere volume
steps: Cube the radius: r³.
Multiply by π.
Multiply by 4/3.
Use π ≈ 3.14.
spherevol.exception: r³ means r × r × r, not 3r. Diameter must be halved before you start.

pythagConv.name: Converse of Pythagoras
pythagConv.phrase: If a² + b² = c², then the triangle is right-angled at the corner between a and b.
steps: Square all three sides.
Check whether the two smaller squares add to the biggest square.
If yes, it is right-angled. If the sum is too small or too big, it is not.
pythagConv.exception: c must be the longest side. Checking the wrong side as “hypotenuse” can fool you.

transform.name: Transformations
transform.phrase: Slide, flip, or turn: translation, reflection, rotation.
steps: Translation: add the same (a, b) to every point.
Reflection in the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). In the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y).
Rotation 90° anticlockwise about the origin: (x, y) → (−y, x).
Rotation 180°: (x, y) → (−x, −y).
transform.exception: Clockwise 90° is (x, y) → (y, −x), the other way. Reflections in other lines need different rules. Translations do not flip or turn the shape.

neg-exponent-one-over.name: Negative exponents
neg-exponent-one-over.phrase: Negative exponent: take one over with a positive power.
neg-exponent-one-over.also: a^(−n) = 1/a^n — the minus flips to a reciprocal, not a negative value.
steps: Rewrite a^(−n) as 1/a^n.
Simplify the positive power in the denominator.
Cancel if possible.
neg-exponent-one-over.exception: x^(−n)=1/x^n for x≠0. A negative exponent does not make the value negative by itself. 2^(−3)=1/8, not −8.

compsupp.name: Complementary & supplementary
compsupp.phrase: C before S: complementary 90°, supplementary 180°. Corner then Straight.
compsupp.also: C for corner (90). S for straight (180).
steps: Complementary: two angles add to 90°.
Supplementary: two angles add to 180°.
C comes before S; 90 comes before 180.
compsupp.exception: They need not be adjacent — they only need to add to 90 or 180.

riserun.name: Rise over run
riserun.phrase: Slope is rise over run — up then along.
steps: Count vertical change (rise).
Count horizontal change (run).
Slope = rise/run.
riserun.exception: Horizontal line: rise 0 → slope 0. Vertical line: run 0 → undefined.

wordkeys8.name: Arithmetic in geometry stories
wordkeys8.phrase: Perimeter altogether adds sides; area is groups of square units; share angles with 180°.
steps: Translate the story to +, −, ×, or ÷.
Use the geometry fact (180°, fence vs carpet).
Solve.
wordkeys8.exception: “Around” is perimeter; “covers” is area — don’t swap formulas.

estimate8.name: Estimate roots & squares
estimate8.phrase: Square a nearby whole; see if your number sits between two squares.
steps: List nearby perfect squares.
Sandwich the number.
Estimate the root between those integers.
estimate8.exception: √50 is a bit more than 7 because 7²=49.

acuteobtuse.name: Angle names
acuteobtuse.phrase: A cute angle is small (acute <90). Obtuse is obese (between 90 and 180).
steps: Acute: less than 90°.
Right: exactly 90°.
Obtuse: between 90° and 180°.
Straight: 180°.
acuteobtuse.exception: Reflex angles are bigger than 180° — past a straight line.

distrib8.name: Distribute into expressions
distrib8.phrase: Outside factor hits every term — like FOIL’s little sibling.
steps: Multiply the outside by each inside term.
Keep signs careful.
Combine like terms if any.
distrib8.exception: If two brackets multiply, use FOIL / grid — not single distribute.

commute8.name: Mental rearrange
commute8.phrase: Flip and regroup to make tens and easy products.
steps: Spot numbers that make 10 or a known product.
Commute/associate to pair them.
Finish mentally.
commute8.exception: With subtraction sitting in the chain, rewrite as adding opposites before regrouping freely.

pythagleg.name: Find a leg
pythagleg.phrase: Leg² = hyp² − other leg² — still Pythagoras.
steps: Square the hypotenuse.
Subtract the other leg squared.
Square-root to get the missing leg.
pythagleg.exception: Hypotenuse is the longest — never subtract a longer square from a shorter and expect a real leg.

vertopp.name: Vertically opposite
vertopp.phrase: X marks the spot: vertically opposite angles are equal.
steps: Find the X made by two crossing lines.
Angles across from each other match.
Neighbors on a straight line add to 180°.
vertopp.exception: Only the opposite pair matches — adjacent angles are supplementary, not equal (unless 90).

scinote8.name: Scientific notation sense
scinote8.phrase: One digit, then a dot, times a power of ten.
steps: Put the point after the first nonzero digit.
Count hops to the original point — that is the exponent.
Positive exponent → big; negative → tiny.
scinote8.exception: The leading number must be ≥1 and <10 (for standard form).

cheat.title: Polygons & space
rows: Two angles that add to 90° (need not touch)
On a line 180°; around a point 360°
